questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 - x - 12$. Verify that $f(x) = 0$ has a root in the interval $4 < x < 5$. Taking $x = 4.5$ as a first approximate root of the equation $f(x) = 0$, use the Newton - Raphson procedure to find a second approximation to the root of the equation, giving the answer to two decimal places. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Verification.** $f$ is a polynomial, so it is continuous on $[4, 5]$.

$$f(4) = 64 - 64 - 4 - 12 = -16 < 0, \qquad f(5) = 125 - 100 - 5 - 12 = 8 > 0.$$

$f(4)$ and $f(5)$ have opposite signs, so by the intermediate value theorem $f(x) = 0$ has a root in $4 < x < 5$.

**Newton - Raphson.** The iteration is $x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$, with $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 8x - 1$.

At $x_0 = 4.5$:

$$f(4.5) = 4.5^3 - 4(4.5)^2 - 4.5 - 12 = 91.125 - 81 - 4.5 - 12 = -6.375,$$

$$f'(4.5) = 3(20.25) - 36 - 1 = 60.75 - 37 = 23.75.$$

$$x_1 = 4.5 - \frac{-6.375}{23.75} = 4.5 + 0.26842\ldots = 4.76842\ldots$$

$$\boxed{x_1 \approx 4.77 \ \text{(2 decimal places)}}$$

This is a second approximation (the first being $4.5$) and it lies inside the interval $4 < x < 5$. (The root itself is about $4.744$; one more iteration from $4.768$ gives $4.744$, so $4.77$ is a sound second approximation.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of a sequence is given by $S_n = 2n^2 + n$. Find

(a) the tenth term of the sequence.

(b) the $n^{th}$ term of the sequence. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The $n$th term is the difference of consecutive sums: $u_n = S_n - S_{n-1}$ for $n \geq 2$, and $u_1 = S_1$.

**(b)** $n$th term. For $n \geq 2$:

$$u_n = (2n^2 + n) - \big[2(n-1)^2 + (n-1)\big] = 2n^2 + n - (2n^2 - 4n + 2 + n - 1) = 2n^2 + n - 2n^2 + 3n - 1 = 4n - 1.$$

For $n = 1$: $u_1 = S_1 = 2 + 1 = 3$, and the formula $4n - 1$ gives $3$, so it holds for $n = 1$ as well.

$$\boxed{u_n = 4n - 1 \quad (n \geq 1)}$$

(This is an arithmetic progression with first term $3$ and common difference $4$.)

**(a)** Tenth term:

$$u_{10} = 4(10) - 1 = 39.$$

Check: $S_{10} = 2(100) + 10 = 210$ and $S_9 = 2(81) + 9 = 171$, so $u_{10} = 210 - 171 = 39$.

$$\boxed{u_{10} = 39}$$
